facts.statement: Duntroonornis parvus, known as the Duntroon penguin, is an extinct species of penguin that lived in New Zealand during the Late Oligocene.
facts.quote: Duntroonornis parvus, also referred to as the Duntroon penguin, is a genus and species of extinct penguin from the Late Oligocene of New Zealand.

facts.statement: This penguin was relatively small, comparable in size to the modern Fiordland crested penguin.
facts.quote: The penguin was relatively small, similar in size to the Fiordland crested penguin.

facts.statement: Brian Marples described the species in 1952 based on a left tarsometatarsus fossil found near Duntroon in the Kokoamu Greensand Formation, close to the border of the Canterbury and Otago regions on New Zealand's South Island.
facts.quote: It was described by Brian Marples in 1952 from fossil material (a left tarsometatarsus) collected near Duntroon, from the Kokoamu Greensand Formation, near the border between the Canterbury and Otago regions of the South Island.

facts.statement: The genus name Duntroonornis translates to "Duntroon bird".
facts.quote: The genus name Duntroonornis means "Duntroon bird".

facts.statement: The specific epithet parvus is Latin for "small".
facts.quote: The specific epithet is the Latin parvus ("small").

facts.statement: Fossils discovered in the Hakataramea Valley might also belong to this species.
facts.quote: Fossils found at the Hakataramea Valley may also be referrable to this species.

facts.statement: Duntroonornis is classified within the order Sphenisciformes and the family Spheniscidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Aves ordo: Sphenisciformes familia: Spheniscidae

facts.statement: The fossil record for Duntroonornis spans the Chattian stage of the Late Oligocene, between 27.3 and 25.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Chattian (27.3 to 25.2 million years ago)
